findings.title: Auth-event sign-out leaves this tab's held trial behind
findings.problem: The auth-state listener handles SIGNED_OUT only by replacing the session. Trial cleanup runs in the initiating tab's sign-out handler, but heldTrial and sessionStorage are tab-local. A sign-out initiated in another tab therefore leaves this tab's held answers intact.
findings.failure_scenario: A student leaves the guest trial for authentication, creating a held copy, but the account handoff has not saved successfully. They sign out from another tab. That tab clears the shared localStorage key, but this tab retains its memory/sessionStorage copy. A subsequent newly created account in this tab satisfies guestHandoff's automatic-merge condition and receives the previous student's answers, XP, and ability updates without consent.
findings.fix: Clear guest and held-trial state in every tab when the auth listener receives SIGNED_OUT, not only when a local button initiates it. Add a multi-tab regression test that retains a held trial, signs out elsewhere, then verifies that another account cannot import it.

findings.title: Guest import does not recognize an already-answered built-in question
findings.problem: Import scoring constructs a question containing only the prefixed guest ID. Unlike the signed-in record path, it provides no verified built-in aliases. Repeat detection consequently works from a guest answer to a later numeric built-in answer, but not in the opposite direction.
findings.failure_scenario: A student correctly answers built-in question 7 in the signed-in offline fallback, producing a numeric log ID of 7. After signing out, they answer that same question in the guest trial and choose Add when signing back into the existing account. Import scoring compares guest-7 against 7 and awards full first-answer XP again, contrary to the once-per-question rule.
findings.fix: Preserve a verified built-in identity in signed-in log rows and use it symmetrically during guest-import scoring. Do not equate arbitrary numeric bank IDs with built-in IDs. Add a regression covering a signed-in built-in answer followed by import of the same guest question.

findings.title: Legacy case aliases require metadata the previous version never saved
findings.problem: The legacy numeric-alias branch requires row.source === "case", but the pre-change CaseStudy call and record implementation never stored source on case answers. Actual legacy case rows therefore cannot match these aliases. The regression test in tests/review3.test.js adds source: "case" to its supposed old rows, so it does not exercise the shipped legacy format.
findings.failure_scenario: An existing save contains a correctly answered sepsis step as { id: 101, cat: "Physiological Adaptation", diff: 3, correct: true }. After upgrading, answering that step under case-sepsis-1 is treated as a first answer and awards another 30 XP. The test claiming that old case steps remain repeats still passes because its fixture contains the newly introduced source field.
findings.fix: Test with the actual pre-change row shape and implement an explicit migration or conservative identity policy for ambiguous legacy numeric rows. Preserve separation from unrelated bank questions, and do not claim legacy repeat preservation using fixtures that older code could not produce.

assessment: Changes required. Cross-tab sign-out can leave trial answers available for import into another account, and XP repeat detection misses two supported histories. This was a static review; tests were not executed.
